title: refactor(react): AdapterCtx and useAdapter are typed by DataSource; react drops its data-objectstack dependency
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9CXkMCRg8Z8RTFcd3HfPqhC)_
Fixes #25917

`@object-ui/react` no longer depends on `@object-ui/data-objectstack`. `AdapterCtx` and `useAdapter()` are typed by the protocol-level `DataSource` from `@object-ui/types`, and a host that installs a concrete adapter declares it once on a new extension point, `AdapterContextRegister` (module augmentation, the same shape as TanStack Router's `Register`). The `enable`-block denial predicate moves to `@object-ui/core`, and the adapter re-exports it unchanged.

Clause-②: yes (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none

## Premise, measured on origin/main 4f7e0414

- The card counted 28 `components` files reaching the concrete adapter. That count is stale: today there are 62 non-test readers of `useAdapter` / `AdapterCtx` (app-shell 41, console 14, components 4, plugin-designer 3).
- 18 of them read `ObjectStackAdapter` members that `DataSource` does not declare: `getClient` (13 files), `probeAppAccess`, `probeMetaItemAccess`, `getConnectionState` / `onConnectionStateChange`, `clearCache`, `queryDataset`. They all sit in app-shell, console and plugin-designer, which already depend on the adapter.
- `isApiAccessDeniedError` is also called inside `data-objectstack`, so `core` is its only single-source home: both `react` and `data-objectstack` depend on `core`.
- The seat chose the route (register augmentation over 18 call-site guards) and amended the claim surface to cover core, data-objectstack and the host declarations.

## What changed

- **`@object-ui/react`**: `AdapterCtx` / `useAdapter()` carry `ContextAdapter`, which resolves to the adapter a host declares on `AdapterContextRegister` and otherwise to `DataSource`. `@object-ui/data-objectstack` moves to `devDependencies`, because one boundary test (`error-message.normalisation-boundary.test.ts`) still reads it. `error-message.ts` imports the predicate from `@object-ui/core`. The README documents the extension point.
- **`@object-ui/core`**: new `utils/api-access-denied.ts` holds `API_ACCESS_DENIED_CODES` and `isApiAccessDeniedError`, moved verbatim with their docblock.
- **`@object-ui/data-objectstack`**: re-exports both names from `@object-ui/core`, so its published face is unchanged, and its internal caller imports the predicate from core.
- **`@object-ui/app-shell`**: `adapter-context-register.ts` declares `ObjectStackAdapter`, and the package entry imports it, so the declaration ships in `dist/index.d.ts`.
- **`@object-ui/plugin-designer`**: the same declaration, imported by the two pages that call `getClient`, so the test type-check program sees it too.
- **sdui**: `core` and `react` re-recorded. `data-objectstack.json` is removed by the generator ("no longer reached"), because the registry walk reached it only through react.

No call site of the 18 changed. Runtime behaviour is unchanged: the context holds the same object.

## Verification (merged main 2409c9c8, head 29b4eeda, all heavy runs under `os-verify-lock`)

- Build: `turbo run build --filter=@object-ui/console`, 71/71 tasks, which includes the Console build.
- `type-check`: core, react, data-objectstack, components, plugin-designer, app-shell and console all exit 0. Console resolves `@object-ui/react` and `@object-ui/app-shell` from `dist`, and its seven files that call `getClient` through app-shell's `useAdapter` compile, so the published app-shell types carry the declaration.
- Published-types probe (one-off, deleted afterwards): a file under `ui/apps/console` that imports type-only from `@object-ui/app-shell` and reads `useAdapter()?.getClient()` exits 0. The same file without the app-shell import exits 2 with TS2339, `Property 'getClient' does not exist on type 'DataSource'` (the compiler prints the type with its `any` argument).
- New pin `AppShellContext.adapterType.pin.test.ts` (13 cases, same tsc harness as `SchemaRendererContext.dataSourceType.pin.test.ts`). Without a declaration, `getClient` and `probeAppAccess` are refused and any `DataSource` may be provided. With a declaration, the host adapter's own member is readable and a bare `DataSource` provider value is refused. CONTROL rows guard against a harness that has degraded to `any`.
- Mutations through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, each restored to the HEAD blob with an empty `git diff HEAD`:
  - Typing the context as `any` turns 2 cases red: the provider check and a CONTROL row.
  - Widening the `DataSource` fallback with `getClient` / `probeAppAccess` turns 3 cases red: both NARROWED rows and the provider row.
- vitest over `packages/react/`, `packages/core/`, `packages/data-objectstack/` and `packages/plugin-designer/`: 480 files and 7238 tests passed, 27 skipped. app-shell's suite is left to CI `Test Core` / Test UI because its runtime is untouched (type declaration only).
- Gates: the 64 families `dispatch-gates --commands` derived were run and reconciled with `--ran`. 63 exit 0. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exits 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET: it reads the whole repo's built output), so it is NOT MEASURED locally and left to CI. `check-adr-0087-registration` verifies `not-required (runtime-interface-only ...#ContextAdapter)`. `check:new-line-citations`: 0 new citations. eslint on the changed files: 0 errors.
- Dogfood: owed once on the final head (Clause-② narrowing). It runs after the next main merge, and the os-dev report carries its reading.

## Acceptance notes

- The changeset carries a FROM → TO fix block, as the seat asked: declare the adapter, or narrow at the call site. `runtime-interface-only` inherits the prescription refusal, and the detector does not read this block as a prescription. The disposition stands on the compiler channel: a reader that needs the declaration gets `TS2339` at its own call site, and no metadata surface moves.
- `plugin-designer` needed the declaration imported by its pages, not only placed under `src/`. Its `tsconfig.test.json` compiles the pages through the test files, and that program never includes a file that nothing imports.
